oneLineDescription: HodlerStation connects projects, creators and communities through Monad missions, indexed on-chain participation and verifiable MON rewards.
description:
HodlerStation turns community participation into verifiable missions and rewards. Projects and creators publish campaigns; participants complete tasks and claim rewards through the existing product workflow.

For Monad, we extended the existing EVM and mission infrastructure instead of creating a separate rewards application. Users select Monad, participate in a mission, submit an on-chain transaction and claim native MON after verification. Mission creation, publishing, approval, budget reservation and recovery reuse the existing host application.

The verified mainnet example uses a CHOG wearable purchase. Envio HyperIndex indexes the existing market's Trade event. The backend matches canonical transaction evidence with the indexed account, contract, token ID, trade direction and quantity before approving the mission. A normal participant then clicks Claim. The existing treasury signer sends MON and the backend finalizes the accounting only after transaction confirmation. Repeated or concurrent claims do not create a second payout.

Dynamic provides a replaceable EVM wallet connection and signing adapter. Real external-wallet authentication and message signing were verified using Dynamic Sandbox; that authentication check is separate from the recorded production mission payout. Envio and Dynamic are isolated behind interfaces so they can be replaced without duplicating mission business logic.

Public-chain evidence records a successful CHOG purchase and one 0.0001 MON payout. The participant's balance increased by exactly 0.0001 MON; the payout reached FINALIZED and the mission reached COMPLETED. A nonexistent hash was rejected and concurrent repeat claims retained one payout.

This repository contains the Monad-specific wallet, indexing and transfer modules plus the deployable Envio indexer. The pre-existing product, user data and private mission/accounting implementation remain private. Source provenance in the host application pins the module revision and file hashes. See submission/evidence.json for transaction and indexer evidence.
goToMarket:
Our first intended users are existing HodlerStation community members and creators, followed by Monad projects that need measurable community participation. We plan to start with small, curated missions with clear budgets and on-chain completion conditions, distribute them through the product and our official X account, and invite project operators to review participation and reward outcomes.

Acquisition is based on a repeatable campaign loop: a project sponsors a mission, creators explain the activity to their communities, users participate, and verified completion leads to a claimable reward. Retention will come from recurring campaigns and visible reward history rather than one-time wallet connections. We will measure mission view-to-join conversion, verified completion, successful claims and repeat participation. We are not claiming unverified partnerships, committed campaign budgets or user-growth metrics.
judgeAccessInstructions:
Open https://app.hodlerstation.xyz and register or sign in through the normal member flow. Select Monad Mainnet in the network selector. Open https://app.hodlerstation.xyz/missions/cmv4wq07u054211aojvtsdwpc to inspect the verified test mission. It is listed on Monad, not BSC, Solana or Monad Testnet.

The recorded participant already completed this mission and cannot receive a second payout. Public evidence can be checked without using that account: purchase https://monadscan.com/tx/0xad512008b8e9b8d6c7c96c809fe3e6f047382caacd6fc58d9129743357ffbc44; payout https://monadscan.com/tx/0x356aea77316864a4ce58c2ea665d6530188c7f22e93a9f0a7a707dbddce0c293.

To reproduce with a new account, connect your own EVM wallet, join the mission before trading, acquire the matching CHOG wearable through the existing market, and submit that account's own transaction hash. CHOG purchase funds and MON gas are required. After the matching Envio event is indexed, the mission approves the participant. Select Claim, review the reward and confirm. Pending settlement is not a failed transfer; wait for completion and inspect the transaction link. Rewards depend on remaining mission capacity and funded budget.

Do not reuse another participant's hash. No admin password, seed phrase or private key is needed. The repository tests run with generated local accounts and do not send mainnet transactions.
envioAnswer:
Envio HyperIndex drives mission completion, rather than serving as a passive analytics integration. Our hosted indexer watches the existing Chog market on Monad chain 143 and materializes each Trade event as MissionTrade. The entity includes chain, contract, transaction hash, block hash/number, log index, account, token ID, buy/sell direction and quantity.

The host first validates canonical on-chain evidence, then the Envio adapter queries the specific indexed event and compares its fields. Missing, mismatched or unavailable indexing cannot authorize completion. A verified event unlocks the existing mission approval and Claim workflow. Native MON payouts are checked through receipts, not misrepresented as ERC-20 Transfer events.

The mainnet example was indexed and used to approve the participant before the 0.0001 MON payout. See config.yaml, schema.graphql, src/handlers.ts, modules/envio-mission-event-source.ts and submission/evidence.json.
dynamicTechnicalDescription:
Dynamic SDK is integrated through modules/dynamic-wallet-provider.tsx and the EIP-1193 bridge in modules/wallet-provider.ts. It supplies wallet connection, message signing, transaction requests and network/account change handling to the host's existing EVM flow. Cancellation rejects pending requests; host-account changes clear the bridge and log out the prior wallet session.

Real external-wallet Dynamic Sandbox authentication, token presence, Monad chain 143 and message-signature verification were observed in the dedicated verification page. Host integration tests cover the bridge and a Dynamic-enabled build. The production MON reward is signed by the server treasury, not by Dynamic. We do not claim that the recorded production payout proves a fresh Dynamic login in that same session.
